Context engineering for coding agents in one minute
I deleted all my MCP servers for CLI tools: saved 40% context
entries.summary: Replacing MCP servers with CLI tools in Claude Code cuts context window usage by ~40%, since MCP tools inject full JSON schemas on every call while CLI-generated bash commands cost roughly 10x fewer tokens with no JSON parsing overhead. Repos like CLI-anything and open-CLI make it easy to wrap any website or API into an agent-callable CLI, and the creator shares a library of 30+ CLI tools covering the most common MCP use cases.

entries.title: My AI Agents Work While I Sleep
entries.summary: This short introduces the AI agent loop concept: rather than single prompts, AI agents run on a goal, self-check their output, and iterate overnight until the task is complete. The presenter positions agentic loops as the automation pattern behind claims that 'AI works for me while I sleep,' with Claude Code cited as the primary tool.

entries.title: AI Cinema is getting TOO real! 🎬 #aigeneration #cinema
entries.summary: Higgsfield AI showcases Cinema Studio 2's AI video directing capabilities, including keyframe-based emotion control, custom character sheet uploads for consistency, and genre/camera presets like Handheld + Horror that completely change a scene's atmosphere. The demo generates a cinematic horror short on a deserted island with character direction and no manual frame editing.

entries.title: Comment “BRAIN” and I’ll send you the guide to add this to your AI setup 👇 The CEO of Y Combinator
entries.summary: Garry Tan (Y Combinator CEO) open-sourced his personal AI second brain 'GBrain' on GitHub, which automatically links people, projects, and companies in notes and runs nightly self-cleanup passes. The video notes GBrain was built for high-volume deal-tracking and has real running costs, while suggesting free alternatives may cover most use cases.

Before You Use Claude Fable 5, Watch This
Biggest AI Controversy At The Moment
entries.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable (Mythos-class) model sparked controversy after being pulled for non-US users due to US government regulations requiring identification verification of foreign nationals — a compliance requirement Anthropic chose not to implement, leading to the model's international removal. Comments note that this move appeared to be connected to Anthropic's earlier refusal to allow the US Department of Defense to use its models for military applications without guardrails, framing the regulation as possible retaliation.
